subject: Post-demo: Hendrix POC — prioritized model shortlist + next actions
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Sinclair <ava.sinclair@hendrixhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Hendrix POC — prioritized model shortlist + next actions

Ava — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + our recommended next steps so your team has a concrete path for the POC.

TL;DR recommended shortlist (ranked by fit for Hendrix use-case: triage + short summarization):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized 8-bit) — Best cost/latency balance for high-throughput triage; very low token cost, median 1.8x faster than 13B alternatives on our 8k windows.
- Vicuna-13B-8k (rw-optimized q4f) — Higher quality on hallucination-sensitive summarization; modest cost increase, median latency ~55% higher than Mistral but still within 250ms p95 on our Dedicated pool.
- Llama-2-70B-chat (float16, constrained prompts) — Best quality ceiling for complex summarization/medical-context preservation when you can accept higher cost; recommend only for heavy post-processing/QA flows.

Why these three: Hendrix needs a hybrid approach — sub-second throughput for the triage path (Mistral) and a higher-quality pass for flagged or sensitive notes (Vicuna or Llama-2-70B). That lets you keep unit costs predictable while retaining a safety valve for quality regressions.

Benchmarks and assets included:
- Benchmarks: see our attached PDF (benchmark_report_hendrix_20280503.pdf) and the Drive folder with raw runs.
- Prompt sets: we packaged the demo prompt set => hendrix_prompt_pack_v1.json (attached) with the triage scaffolds and the QA guardrails we used in the demo.

Open concerns to validate in the POC:
- Latency SLOs at peak: the triage path must meet 200–300ms p95 under Hendrix traffic profile; we can simulate with our load harness but need your request distribution.
- Hallucination sensitivity: we flagged two prompt examples from the demo where the 7B family produced overconfident summaries — wants further eval with your labeled ground truth.
- Data residency / logging: confirm retention window and whether you need token-level logs (we can mask and redact).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) We run a 48-hour production-like run on your sample traffic (we need an export or a small replay set).
2) We deliver per-model scorecards (F1/ROUGE for your labeled set, latency percentiles, cost per 1k tokens).
3) Joint review meeting (30 min) next week to pick the primary model and fallback policy.

If that plan looks right, I’ll ask Karthik to schedule the run and drop the benchmark links.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: hendrix_prompt_pack_v1.json (prompt set, 20 prompts), benchmark_report_hendrix_20280503.pdf (summary + raw logs)
From: Ava Sinclair <ava.sinclair@hendrixhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@hendrixhealth.com
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hendrix POC — prioritized model shortlist + next actions

Thanks Rachel — this is exactly the kind of clarity we needed. A few quick notes from our side: 
- The triage SLO target is 250ms p95 (conservative) for the org-wide triage queue; during business hours peak we see ~120 req/s.
- We can provide a 2-day replay of redacted traffic for the 48-hour run — security will pull logs Monday.
- Hallucination examples: I’ve attached two informal labels in the Drive folder; want to see how each model performs on those.

Question: what control do we have over the fallback policy? Ideally we want an automated path: if the triage model confidence < threshold, send to higher quality model and create an audit ticket. Can Redwood handle that out-of-the-box?

Thanks — Ava
Ava Sinclair | Head of Product, Hendrix Health
ava.sinclair@hendrixhealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Sinclair <ava.sinclair@hendrixhealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 04 May 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hendrix POC — prioritized model shortlist + next actions

Ava — quick answers, and I dropped the raw benchmark runs to the Drive link in Rachel’s note.

On fallback policies: yes — Redwood supports policy-based routing. Example configuration we recommend for Hendrix:
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (q8) for all triage requests.
- Fallback trigger: model confidence < 0.6 OR prompt classification tag = "sensitive" OR a heuristic that routes >1 entity with medical terminology.
- Fallback target: Vicuna-13B-8k (q4f) with a short-context retry.
- Escalation: If Vicuna confidence < 0.7, route to Llama-2-70B-chat for human-in-the-loop review, and create an audit ticket in Hendrix Jira via webhook.

Benchmarks summary (high level):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (q8): cost ~ $0.45 / 1k tokens; p95 latency 220ms (dedicated small pool); summary quality (ROUGE-L) baseline: 0.62 on your sample set.
- Vicuna-13B-8k (q4f): cost ~ $1.30 / 1k tokens; p95 latency 340ms; ROUGE-L: 0.72.
- Llama-2-70B-chat: cost ~ $6.40 / 1k tokens (float16); p95 latency 1.2s; ROUGE-L: 0.81.

Notes on the hallucination cases: Mistral tended to omit context when prompts contained long quoted notes. We recommend prompt-scoped context windows (trim non-essential history) + our guardrail filters (we included examples in hendrix_prompt_pack_v1.json).

I’ve attached the full benchmark PDF and the prompt pack to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HendrixPOCBenchmarks. You should see per-prompt breakdowns and raw traces.

Next actions from Redwood side (I’ll own scheduling):
- Set up the replay (Rachel: can you share replay instructions for Hendrix infra?).
- Kick off a 48-hour sim run Monday morning once we have the replay.
- Deliver the model scorecards within 48 hours of run completion.

Ben — can you confirm pricing guidance for the POC run and any temporary credits?

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hendrix POC — prioritized model shortlist + next actions

Ava — quick commercial note: for the POC we can cover up to $2k in run costs (credits applied to the Redwood account) to get you comfortable with the performance profile. If the run exceeds that, we’ll provide an itemized run estimate upfront and pause so you can approve.

Operationally, we recommend the following billing guardrails for the trial:
- Tag the replay runs with project:hendrix-poc so we can isolate costs and telemetry.
- Enable short retention for token logs during the test (7 days) and redact PHI fields by default. We’ll collect only the metrics needed for scorecards unless you opt-in to full logs.

I’ll get the credits applied; Rachel, once replay is uploaded and you confirm Monday start, I’ll kick it off.

Best — Ben
